title: Amplitude and Period of a Vertically Scaled Sine
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For the curve $y=3\sin x$, state the amplitude of the oscillation and the length of one full cycle.

steps.title: Match the Standard Form
steps.explanation: Reading off coefficients gives $A=3$ in front and $B=1$ inside the argument.
steps.why: The template $y=A\sin(Bx)$ separates vertical from horizontal effects.

steps.title: Compute the Amplitude
steps.explanation: The curve swings between $y=-3$ and $y=3$, three times taller than the unit sine.
steps.why: Amplitude is the absolute vertical coefficient, measuring height from the midline.

steps.title: Compute the Period
steps.explanation: With $B=1$ the horizontal spacing is untouched, so one full wave still takes $2\pi$.
steps.why: The horizontal scaling factor $B$ divides the base period of sine.
